title: First positions: GTA6 and SI
text:
Plan started with 1.99 SOL ($201). Two positions, one third of the plan each, and the rest kept in SOL for the next good setup.

GTA6 ($7.2M market cap, 25.8K holders, $401K liquidity): a meme built around the GTA VI release on November 19, after this plan's first review window, so the story should keep building. Our anti-rug check found no group of top holders funded by the same wallet. The same brain bought it for the live desk yesterday.

SI ($14.3M, 52K holders, top 10 hold 11%): real, irregular trading volume worth 34% of its value per day, up 45% in three days and 20% below its weekly high. Anti-rug: clean (largest common-funder group holds 1.7%).

Devil's advocate: GTA6 is up 56% in 24 hours, so we are buying after a run, not on a pullback; a 30% stop can fill lower if it drops fast. SI's creator has launched about 7,500 tokens, the profile of a token factory, even though the holders look spread out. We accept it with a 30% stop on each and modest size, so a worst case costs about a fifth of the plan.

title: Selling DOAS: the automatic buy broke a rule
text:
The automatic brain bought DOAS at 16:07 ART with idle cash. That was a filter mistake, not a bet: DOAS has been on our fabricated-volume list since October 27 (bots trading the same amount every hour), and the scan data was inconsistent (−98% in 24 hours, 2% of its 3-day high). The filter blocked overheated tokens but not collapsed ones.

Selling now, close to the entry price; the cost is the round-trip fee and slippage (about 3%, roughly $2). The brain is fixed: it now only buys a healthy pullback (55–90% of the 3-day high, between −40% and +60% in 24 hours), with daily volume of at least 30% of market cap, 1,000+ holders, a scan less than 2.5 hours old, and a fabricated-volume blacklist.
